topic: Simple and Multiple Linear Regression, Ridge Regression
q: [NAT] Given data {(-1, 1), (2, -5), (3, 5)} of the form (x, y), fit a model y = wx using linear least-squares regression. The optimal value of w is ____ (rounded off to three decimal places).

topic: Simple and Multiple Linear Regression, Ridge Regression
q: [NAT] For a supervised learning task, the objective function being minimized is f_w(x) = wx, where x is the input and w is the parameter. Stochastic Gradient Descent with learning rate 0.10 is used for updates. At the end of iteration i, w = 10.00. Taking x = 10.00 as the input for iteration (i+1), the value of w at the end of iteration (i+1) is ____ (rounded off to two decimal places).

topic: Simple and Multiple Linear Regression, Ridge Regression
q: [NAT] Linear Ridge Regression learns y_pred = w^T x (w, x in R^2) with Mean Absolute Error as the prediction error and regularizer weight 0.20. At an intermediate training step w = [-3.00, 4.00]^T. For the next input x = [1.00, 2.00]^T, the true relation is y_true = x1 + x2. The value of the overall regularized loss function for this instance is ____ (rounded off to two decimal places).

Match the items in Column 1 with Column 2: (p) Principal Component Analysis, (q) Naive Bayes Classification, (r) Logistic Regression with (i) Discriminative Model, (ii) Dimensionality Reduction, (iii) Generative Model. Options: (A) p-iii, q-i, r-ii (B) p-ii, q-i, r-iii (C) p-ii, q-iii, r-i (D) p-iii, q-ii, r-i.
[NAT] Let f: R -> R be the sigmoid function f(x) = 1/(1 + e^(-x)). The value of the derivative of f at the x where f(x) = 0.4 is ____ (rounded off to two decimal places).

topic: k-Nearest Neighbours, Naive Bayes, Linear Discriminant Analysis
q: Given a dataset with K binary-valued attributes (where K > 2) for a two-class classification task, the number of parameters to be estimated for learning a naive Bayes classifier is: (A) 2K + 1 (B) 2^K + 1 (C) 2^(K+1) + 1 (D) K^2 + 1.

topic: k-Nearest Neighbours, Naive Bayes, Linear Discriminant Analysis
q: For a binary classification dataset, let S_B and S_W (both in R^(d x d)) be the between-class and within-class scatter (covariance) matrices. The Fisher linear discriminant u* maximizes J(u) = (u^T S_B u)/(u^T S_W u). If lambda = J(u*), S_W is non-singular and S_B is non-zero, then (u*, lambda) must satisfy: (A) S_W^(-1) S_B u* = lambda u* (B) S_W u* = lambda S_B u* (C) S_B S_W u* = lambda u* (D) u*^T u* = lambda^2.

topic: k-Nearest Neighbours, Naive Bayes, Linear Discriminant Analysis
q: [NAT] A two-dimensional dataset of 5 labelled data points from two classes (circles and squares) is given, along with a diamond-shaped query point; Euclidean distance measures the distance between points. The minimum odd value of k in the k-nearest neighbour algorithm for which the diamond-shaped point is assigned the label 'square' is ____.

topic: k-Nearest Neighbours, Naive Bayes, Linear Discriminant Analysis
q: [NAT] A naive Bayes classifier solves a two-class problem with class labels y1, y2 and priors P(y1) = 1/3, P(y2) = 2/3. For a specific feature vector x in a discrete feature space, P(x|y1) = 3/4 and P(x|y2) = 1/4. The probability of misclassifying x is ____ (rounded off to two decimal places).

topic: k-Nearest Neighbours, Naive Bayes, Linear Discriminant Analysis
q: [MSQ] Match each Task with the Algorithm that solves it: T1 Clustering, T2 Classification, T3 Sampling, T4 Feature Extraction with A1 Markov Chain Monte Carlo, A2 K-Medoid, A3 Linear Discriminant Analysis, A4 Naive Bayes. Which of the following options is/are correct matching(s)? (A) T1:A4, T2:A3, T3:A1, T4:A2 (B) T1:A2, T2:A4, T3:A1, T4:A3 (C) T1:A3, T2:A4, T3:A1, T4:A2 (D) T1:A4, T2:A2, T3:A1, T4:A3.

Dataset of six points: x1=[1,0], x2=[0,1], x3=[0,-1], x4=[-1,0], x5=[2,2], x6=[-2,-2], with labels y1=y2=y5=1 and y3=y4=y6=-1. A hard margin linear support vector machine is trained on this dataset. Which ONE of the following sets is a possible set of support vectors? (A) {x1, x2, x5} (B) {x3, x4, x5} (C) {x4, x5} (D) {x1, x2, x3, x4}.

[MSQ] Four figures (i)-(iv) show datasets of two-dimensional features with two classes denoted by circles and squares. Which of the following is/are TRUE? (A) (i) is linearly separable (B) (ii) is linearly separable (C) (iii) is linearly separable (D) (iv) is linearly separable.

[MSQ] Design a linear binary classifier f(x) = sign(w^T x + b), x in R^2, on the training data: Class-1 = {(2,0), (0,2), (2,2)}, Class-2 = {(0,0)}. The hard-margin support vector machine (SVM) formulation is solved to obtain w and b. Which of the following options is/are correct? (A) w = (4,4) and b = 1 (B) The number of support vectors is 3 (C) The margin is sqrt(2) (D) Training accuracy is 98%.

[MSQ] In a two-class problem in R^d with labels red and green and class means mu_red, mu_green, a classifier computes f(x) = ||mu_red - x||^2 - ||mu_green - x||^2 and assigns label red if f(x) < 0, else green. Which of the following statements is/are correct? (A) The sample x = 0 is assigned green if ||mu_red|| < ||mu_green|| (B) f is a linear function of x (C) f(x) = w^T x + b, where w and b are functions of mu_red and mu_green (D) f is a quadratic polynomial in x.

[NAT] Ten international cricket games between teams Green and Blue are given with attributes Pitch (S = spin-friendly, F = pace-friendly) and Format (O = one-day, T = test) and target Winner: (S,T,Green), (S,T,Blue), (F,O,Blue), (S,O,Blue), (F,T,Green), (F,O,Blue), (S,O,Green), (F,T,Blue), (F,O,Blue), (S,O,Green). A decision-tree model is built to predict outcomes of future games. The computed InformationGain(C, Pitch) with respect to the target is ____ (rounded off to two decimal places).

You are training a classifier for a 10-class classification problem. Each input is a 512-dimensional vector. There are 1000 samples, of which the first 100 will be used for testing. Leave-One-Out-Cross-Validation (LOOCV) is used for selection of the classifier model before testing. Which option is the correct number of validation splits that will be generated? (A) 10 (B) 512 (C) 900 (D) 1000.

Which of the following statements is true for Ridge Regression? (A) The regularizer guards against scenarios where the model works well for test data but poorly for training data (B) The regularizer uses the L1 norm (C) Ridge Regression aims to reduce the number of parameters that have negative values (D) The regularizer may increase the bias of the model, but it helps in reducing the variance in predictions.

topic: Multi-Layer Perceptron and Feed-Forward Neural Networks
q: Two neural networks (Figures 1 and 2) use ReLU activation ReLU(z) = max{0, z} with all biases set to 0; the connection weights are shown in the figures, with unknown weights p, q, r in Figure 2. For what values of p, q, r are the two NNs equivalent when x1, x2, x3 are positive? (A) p=36, q=24, r=24 (B) p=24, q=24, r=36 (C) p=18, q=36, r=24 (D) p=36, q=36, r=36.

topic: Multi-Layer Perceptron and Feed-Forward Neural Networks
q: A linear classifier y = sign(f(x; w, b)), f(x; w, b) = w^T x + b, is trained by updating w_new = w_old + y_n x_n and b_new = b_old + y_n whenever sign(f(x_n; w_old, b_old)) does not equal y_n. For the case (x_n, +1) with f(x_n; w_old, b_old) < 0, which one is correct? (A) f(x_n; w_new, b_new) > f(x_n; w_old, b_old) (B) f(x_n; w_new, b_new) < f(x_n; w_old, b_old) (C) f(x_n; w_new, b_new) = f(x_n; w_old, b_old) (D) y_n f(x_n; w_old, b_old) > 1.

topic: Multi-Layer Perceptron and Feed-Forward Neural Networks
q: The neural network shown in the figure has inputs u, v; weights a, b, c, d, e, f; output y; and ReLU activation R(x) = max(0, x) at its neurons. Given u = 2, v = 3, a = 1, b = 1, c = 1, d = -1, e = 4, f = -1, which one is correct? (A) dy/da = 8, dy/df = 0 (B) dy/da = 1, dy/df = 0 (C) dy/da = 1, dy/df = -1 (D) dy/da = 2, dy/df = -1.

topic: Multi-Layer Perceptron and Feed-Forward Neural Networks
q: [MSQ] Which of the following statements is/are correct about the rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation function defined as ReLU(x) = max(x, 0), x in R? (A) ReLU is continuous everywhere (B) ReLU is differentiable everywhere (C) ReLU is not differentiable at x = 0 (D) ReLU(x) = ReLU(ax) for all a in R.

topic: Multi-Layer Perceptron and Feed-Forward Neural Networks
q: [NAT] A fully-connected feed-forward multi-layer perceptron has 30 neurons in the input layer, two hidden layers with 4 and 3 neurons respectively, and one neuron in the output layer. No bias parameters are used. The number of learnable parameters in the MLP is ____ (integer).

Euclidean distance based k-means clustering was run on a dataset of 100 points with k = 3. If the points [1,1] and [-1,1] are both part of cluster 3, which ONE of the following points is necessarily also part of cluster 3? (A) [0,0] (B) [0,2] (C) [2,0] (D) [0,1].

The (i, j)-th entry of the given table is the distance between points x_i and x_j for x1..x5: d(x1,x2)=1, d(x1,x3)=4, d(x1,x4)=3, d(x1,x5)=6, d(x2,x3)=3, d(x2,x4)=5, d(x2,x5)=3, d(x3,x4)=2, d(x3,x5)=5, d(x4,x5)=1. Single linkage clustering is performed on these data points. Which ONE option is the correct representation of the clusters produced (dendrogram figures)?

[MSQ] Let C1, C2 be two sets of objects and D(x, y) a dissimilarity measure, with DIS-1(C1,C2) = max over x in C1, y in C2 of D(x,y) and DIS-2(C1,C2) = min over x in C1, y in C2 of D(x,y). Which of the following statements is/are correct? (A) Single Linkage Clustering uses DIS-1 (B) Single Linkage Clustering uses DIS-2 (C) Complete Linkage Clustering uses DIS-2 (D) Complete Linkage Clustering uses DIS-1.

Four points in 3-D space: P1=[2,3,-1], P2=[3,1,1], P3=[5,-2,3], P4=[3,3,3]. Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering is applied using Manhattan Distance as the metric. Which option indicates the two points that will be merged first? (A) P1, P2 (B) P2, P3 (C) P3, P4 (D) P2, P4.

[NAT] Let u = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]^T, and let sigma1, sigma2, sigma3, sigma4, sigma5 be the singular values of the matrix M = u u^T (u^T being the transpose of u). The value of sum of sigma_i for i = 1 to 5 is ____.

[NAT] Let D = {x(1), ..., x(n)} be a dataset of n observations, each x(i) in R^100, with sum of x(i) = 0. The covariance matrix computed from D has eigenvalues lambda_i = 100^(2-i), 1 <= i <= 100. Let u in R^100 be the unit direction of maximum variance. The value of (1/n) times sum over i of (u^T x(i))^2 is ____ (integer).

For a classification problem, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) has been used to reduce the dimensionality of a feature space from 100 to 10. Which option is true about the angle theta between the first and the tenth principal components? (A) theta = 0 degrees (B) theta = 90 degrees (C) 90 < theta <= 180 degrees (D) 0 < theta < 90 degrees.

[NAT] Let A = (I_n - (1/n) 1 1^T), where 1 = (1, 1, ..., 1)^T in R^n and I_n is the identity matrix of order n. The value of max over S of x^T A x, where S = {x in R^n : x^T x = 1}, is ____ (integer).

Consider performing depth-first search (DFS) on an undirected, unweighted graph G starting at vertex s; d[u] is the length of the shortest path from s to u. Let (u, v) be an edge with d[u] < d[v]. If the edge (u, v) is explored first in the direction from u to v during the DFS, then (u, v) becomes a ____ edge. (A) tree (B) cross (C) back (D) gray.

In a state space the start state is number 1, and the successor function for state n returns states n+1 and n+2. States in the unexpanded list are expanded in ascending order of numbers, and previously expanded states are not re-added. Which ONE statement about breadth-first search (BFS) and depth-first search (DFS) is true when reaching goal state number 6? (A) BFS expands more states than DFS (B) DFS expands more states than BFS (C) Both expand an equal number of states (D) Neither reaches goal state 6.

[NAT] Consider a directed graph G = (V, E), V = {0, 1, ..., 100}, E = {(i, j) : 0 < j - i <= 2}. The adjacency list of each vertex is in decreasing order of vertex number, and depth-first search (DFS) is performed starting at vertex 0. The number of vertices that will be discovered after vertex 50 is ____ (integer).
Which of the following algorithms is NOT an example of uninformed search? (A) Breadth First Search (B) Depth First Search (C) A* Search (D) Depth-limited Search.

Let G = (V, E) be a directed graph (may contain cycles, no self-loops, need not be strongly connected), and G_R the graph obtained by reversing all edge directions without changing vertices. BFS or DFS from any given vertex v visits exactly the reachable vertices from v. Which of the following statements must always be true, regardless of the structure of G? (A) If u is reachable in the BFS of G_R from v, then u is also reachable in the DFS of G from v (B) In G_R, BFS from v visits exactly the same set of vertices as DFS from v in G (C) The order of vertices visited in BFS of G_R from v is the reverse of the order in DFS of G from v (D) If u is reachable in the DFS of G from v, then v is also reachable in the BFS of G_R from u.
Let h1 and h2 be two admissible heuristics used in A* search. Which ONE of the following expressions is always an admissible heuristic? (A) h1 + h2 (B) h1 x h2 (C) h1/h2 (h2 not 0) (D) |h1 - h2|.

The state graph shows the action cost along the edges and the heuristic function h associated with each state (nodes S, A, B, C, D, E, G with given h values; G is the goal). A* algorithm is applied using a priority queue to store the frontier. In what sequence are the nodes expanded? (A) S,A,E,C,B,D,G (B) S,E,A,C,B,D,G (C) S,A,E,B,C,D,G (D) S,A,B,E,C,D,G.

In adversarial search, alpha-beta pruning can be applied to game trees of any depth, where alpha is the (m) value choice formed so far at any choice point along the path for the MAX player and beta is the (n) value choice formed so far for the MIN player. Which choice of (m) and (n) makes the statement valid? (A) m = highest, n = highest (B) m = lowest, n = highest (C) m = highest, n = lowest (D) m = lowest, n = lowest.

Consider game trees Tree-1 and Tree-2, where the first level is a MAX agent and the second level a MIN agent; utility values (including unknowns x and y) are at the leaf/square nodes (Tree-1 root A has children with values 2, x, 1; Tree-2 node E has children 5, y, 2). For what ranges of x and y will the right child of node B and the right child of node E be pruned by the alpha-beta pruning algorithm? (A) x in [1, inf) and y in (-inf, 2] (B) x in (-inf, 2] and y in (-inf, 5] (C) x in (-inf, 2] and y in [2, inf) (D) x in [1, inf) and y in (-inf, 5].

[NAT] In the game tree for a two-player turn-taking minimax game (figure), MAX starts at the root and has three strategies 1, 2, 3; MIN then also has three strategies 1, 2, 3; the game ends there. Terminal nodes show the utility of each game state, and both players always take optimal strategies. At the root, the best strategy for MAX is ____ (integer).

topic: Propositional Logic and Predicate Logic (AI section)
q: Let x and y be two propositions. Which of the following statements is a tautology / are tautologies? (A) (not x AND y) => (y => x) (B) (x AND not y) => (not x => y) (C) (not x AND y) => (not x => y) (D) (x AND not y) => (y => x).

topic: Propositional Logic and Predicate Logic (AI section)
q: [MSQ] Let game(ball, rugby) be true if the ball is used in rugby, and shape(ball, round) be true if the ball is round. Sentences: s1: for all ball, NOT game(ball, rugby) => shape(ball, round); s2: for all ball, NOT shape(ball, round) => game(ball, rugby); s3: for all ball, game(ball, rugby) => NOT shape(ball, round); s4: for all ball, shape(ball, round) => NOT game(ball, rugby). Which choice(s) is/are logical representations of the assertion 'All balls are round except balls used in rugby'? (A) s1 AND s3 (B) s1 AND s2 (C) s2 AND s3 (D) s3 AND s4.

topic: Propositional Logic and Predicate Logic (AI section)
q: Let p and q be any two propositions: S1: p -> q, S2: NOT p AND q, S3: NOT p OR q, S4: NOT p OR NOT q (AND = conjunction, OR = disjunction, NOT = negation). Which one option is correct (== denotes logical equivalence)? (A) S1 == S3 (B) S2 == S3 (C) S2 == S4 (D) S1 == S4.

topic: Propositional Logic and Predicate Logic (AI section)
q: Assume a Creative (C) person will Succeed (S) if the person is also Disciplined (D), but will not succeed otherwise. Statements: (i) C AND S <=> D; (ii) C => (S <=> D); (iii) C <=> ((D => S) OR NOT S). Which option is correct? (A) Both (i) and (ii) are TRUE (B) Only (ii) is TRUE (C) Both (ii) and (iii) are TRUE (D) Only (iii) is TRUE.

topic: Propositional Logic and Predicate Logic (AI section)
q: [MSQ] Let P(x) be a predicate. Which of the following statements is/are NOT valid in first-order logic? (A) forall x P(x) => exists x P(x) (B) exists x P(x) => forall x P(x) (C) exists x P(x) <=> forall x P(x) (D) forall x P(x) => exists x NOT P(x).

topic: Reasoning under Uncertainty — Conditional Independence, Variable Elimination, Sampling
q: Five random variables U, V, W, X, Y have joint distribution P(U, V, W, X, Y) = P(U) P(V) P(W|U,V) P(X|W) P(Y|W). Which ONE of the following statements is FALSE? (A) Y is conditionally independent of V given W (B) X is conditionally independent of U given W (C) U and V are conditionally independent given W (D) Y and X are conditionally independent given W.

topic: Reasoning under Uncertainty — Conditional Independence, Variable Elimination, Sampling
q: [NAT] A Bayesian network of four Bernoulli random variables U, V, W, Z has CPTs: P(U=0) = P(U=1) = 0.5; P(V=0|U) = P(V=1|U) = 0.5 for both U values; P(W=0|U=0) = 1, P(W=1|U=0) = 0, P(W=0|U=1) = 0, P(W=1|U=1) = 1; P(Z=0|V=0,W=0) = 0.5, P(Z=1|V=0,W=0) = 0.5, P(Z=0|V=0,W=1) = 1, P(Z=0|V=1,W=0) = 1, P(Z=0|V=1,W=1) = 0.5. The value of P(U=1, V=1, W=1, Z=1) is ____ (rounded off to three decimal places).

topic: Reasoning under Uncertainty — Conditional Independence, Variable Elimination, Sampling
q: [MSQ] Which of the following statements is/are correct in a Bayesian network? (A) Variable elimination is an approximate inference algorithm (B) Gibbs sampling is an exact inference algorithm (C) Variable elimination is used to determine conditional probabilities (D) Rejection sampling is an approximate inference algorithm.

topic: Reasoning under Uncertainty — Conditional Independence, Variable Elimination, Sampling
q: [NAT] A clinic tests for disease D. If a person suffers from D, the test is positive 80% of the time and negative 20%; if a person does not suffer from D, the test is positive 10% and negative 90%. The disease D occurs in 30% of the general population. If a person tests positive for D, the probability that he/she actually suffers from D is ____ (rounded off to two decimal places).
